title: Watch the Low Stool  (低い踏み台に気をつけて)

segments.t: 火曜日の夕方、カフェコーナー奥の暖かいキッチンでタルト生地が網の上で冷まされるなか、大きな銅のやかんを取ろうとテッサが低い木の踏み台に上がります。ちょうどそこへハンナがメニューを手に入ってきます。まずは場面を聴いてみましょう。
Tessa, wait, let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Hannah, I just need the big teapot... ouch!
Tessa! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair, do not stand up!
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
Toes move fine, nothing broken, just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
No, no, Hannah! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you will not walk for two weeks!
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
Look around this house, Tessa: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
突然のアクシデントから頼もしい逆転の発想へつながる二人のやり取りを、一文ずつ表現ごとに見ていきます。
Tessa, wait, let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
'テッサ、待って、上の棚に手を伸ばすあいだ私がその木の踏み台を押さえているわ！'
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Hannah, I just need the big teapot... ouch!
'この小さな踏み台には週に十回も上がっているのよ、ハンナ。大きなティーポットが要るだけなの……いたっ！'
Tessa! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair, do not stand up!
'テッサ！私の腕につかまって！すぐこの椅子に座って、立ち上がらないで！'
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
'ああ……降りようとしたとき、右の靴が下の踏み桟（さん）で滑っちゃったの！'
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
'そっと靴を脱がせるわね。私のために足の指をくねくね動かせる？'
Toes move fine, nothing broken, just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
'指は大丈夫、折れてはいないわ。足首の外側を鋭くぐきっとひねっただけ。'
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
'清潔なタオルに冷たい氷を包んでくるあいだ、二脚目のこの椅子に足を上げたままにしておいて。'
No, no, Hannah! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
'だめよ、ハンナ！明日は水曜日なの！レンズ豆のスープもレモンタルト二十個も仕上げなくちゃならないのに！'
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you will not walk for two weeks!
'今夜その腫れた足首で立ったら、二週間歩けなくなるわよ！'
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
'私が椅子に座っていたら、いったい誰が水曜日の焼きたてパンとレモンカードを焼いて作るの？！'
Look around this house, Tessa: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
'テッサ、この家の仲間を見回してごらん。あなたには六人分の手と、大きな声一つがあるじゃない！'
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
'待って……私にクッションの上に座って、みんなに命令を出しまくれっていうの？！'
では、今の表現を思い浮かべながら、緊迫と温かさの詰まった場面をもう一度聴き直してみましょう。
Tessa, wait, let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the top shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Hannah, I just need the big teapot... ouch!
Tessa! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair, do not stand up!
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes for me?
Toes move fine, nothing broken, just a sharp twist on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap cold ice in a clean towel.
No, no, Hannah! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty lemon tarts to finish!
If you stand on a swollen ankle tonight, you will not walk for two weeks!
Who will bake Wednesday's fresh bread and lemon curd if I sit in a chair?!
Look around this house, Tessa: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
骨は折れておらず、ひねった足首にも冷たい氷が当てられました。そしてハンナにはもう、水曜日の朝を乗り切る救出プランができています！次回をお楽しみに。
See you later!
